text: Wool blocks vibrations. A single wool block under your feet stops a sculk sensor from hearing you walk.
A goat horn only drops when a goat rams a solid block. If it rams you instead, you get knocked off the mountain and nothing else.
Throw a snowball next to a Warden and it walks to where the snowball landed, not to where you are.
Ancient debris is thickest around Y=15, which is why the fast way to farm it is beds at that depth rather than a pickaxe.
Axolotls play dead the moment they take damage, and they only spawn in lush caves.
A fox will carry a Totem of Undying in its mouth, and the totem still saves the fox when it dies.
Break a bee nest without Silk Touch and the bees come out angry, chasing you for twenty blocks or more.
The End credits poem was written by Julian Gough. It runs past 1,500 words and Mojang has never shortened it.
The title screen has a 1-in-10,000 chance of misspelling the game's own name as “Minceraft”.
A full moon raises the regional difficulty and lets slimes spawn on the surface, which is why night three feels harder than night two.

Herobrine: white eyes, no pupils, in every cursed screenshot since 2010. Mojang has said more than once that he was never in the game, and every sighting traced back to a mod, a texture pack, or a hoax.
The Far Lands. Players treated it as the edge of the world for years. It was a real terrain bug 12.5 million blocks out; Mojang removed it, and the stories outlived the place.
The dragon egg. Every few months someone posts a method to hatch it. You cannot: it is a trophy block, and every method is either a mod or someone having fun with you.
The Herobrine altar: a 3×3 of gold blocks, netherrack on top, redstone torches around it. The recipe comes from a 2010 server plugin, and on a clean client it is just a pile of expensive blocks.

Steve is the last human. Mineshafts nobody built, villages with no villagers, a world full of ruins: fans built an entire post-apocalypse out of world generation, and the game has never said a word about it.
There is a persistent story that Endermen speak reversed English. The sounds really are reversed vocal recordings, which is probably where the story started.
Cursed seeds. Every few months someone posts a world seed that is “haunted”. Every one that has been checked turned out to be a texture pack, a mod, or a friend on the server.
Never dig straight down. Every veteran says it, and every veteran has a lava story that proves it.
Torches on the right as you head in, so you can find the way back out.
Carry a water bucket. It is a ladder, a fire extinguisher and a fall breaker at the same time.
The Strange Capsule event drops a pod on your farm. Days later it cracks open and an alien silhouette appears outside at night.
You can put hats on your horse, your children, and the alien. The horse one is the only genuinely useful one.
You can also put a hat on a sea urchin in a fish tank. Nobody knows why this is allowed, but it is.
The Trash Bear turns up in Year 3 and cleans the trash around town, but only after you feed it.
Grandpa's evaluation lights four candles. Get all four and the Statue of Perfection drops iridium ore on your farm every morning.
Krobus will move in as a roommate at ten hearts. He will not marry you, and he keeps his own room.
The Sewers key comes from the museum: donate 60 items and Gunther hands it over.
Sprinklers water at 6:00, before you wake up, so a crop planted later in the day waits until tomorrow for its first drink.
Qi's Walnut Room needs 100 golden walnuts, and several of the best items in the game are only sold there.
Crows only eat uncovered crops, and a scarecrow covers a fixed radius. Most “why is everything eaten” problems are a layout problem, not bad luck.
Aged wine takes two full seasons in a cask to reach iridium, which is slower than almost everyone expects on their first cellar.
The Traveling Cart merchant. Players have argued for years that she is the Witch in disguise, because both sell things nobody else stocks. ConcernedApe has never confirmed it.
You can marry Krobus. You cannot: at ten hearts he moves in as a roommate, and the game is careful to call it something else.
Your pet can die. It cannot. The cat or dog never starves, never gets sick, and will still be asleep in the same spot in Year 10.
Grandpa's ghost is watching the farm. The shrine is literally the scoreboard, and the four candles are Grandpa grading how you played.
There is a long-running story that the Dwarf and Krobus are the last two survivors of a war between their peoples. The dialogue hints at it and never says it.
The fifth candle. People insist there is a hidden way to light a fifth candle on the shrine. There are four, and the statue only counts the four.
Save your first Prismatic Shard. Everyone who spent it on a sword regrets it by Year 3.
Incubate your first Dinosaur Egg instead of selling it.
Keep a chest with one of everything for the Community Center. You will need it, and you will not want to go back for it.
The Torch God is real. Place enough torches in one underground spot and the world answers.
Shimmer, added in 1.4.4, can downgrade items: drop a crafted thing in and get the components back.
The Tax Collector is the only NPC you have to free from the Underworld.
The Guide is not decoration. Stand next to him with a material and he lists everything it can make, including recipes you have not unlocked yet.
Pylons need at least two nearby NPCs, and cramming too many into one spot drops their happiness, which raises every price they charge.
The Dungeon is sealed until Skeletron dies, but the bookshelves in the entrance hall can hold a Water Bolt, so you can walk out with a spell before the fight.
Every Demon Altar you smash with the Pwnhammer seeds more hardmode ore into the world. Smash too few and the world stays poor.
Fallen stars become Mana Crystals, and one crystal is +20 maximum mana. Ten of them is the whole bar.
The Merchant only moves in once you have 50 silver and a valid house, which is why some players wait far too long for a shop.
Fishing crates can contain ores from biomes you have not reached yet, so a fishing afternoon is sometimes the fastest way past a tier.

The Guide is the Wall of Flesh. The summon item is a Guide Voodoo Doll thrown into lava, and the thing that rises wears the Guide's face. Fans have argued about what that means for a decade; the game never explains.
Red's Wings and the dev armour sets. They sit in the game files, they are not obtainable in normal play, and for years people traded rumours about how to get them.
The Lihzahrd Temple door. Before Plantera, everyone has tried to bomb, drill, or hoik through it. Some old versions actually let you.
The Dungeon Guardian follows you home. It does not, but it follows further than people expect, which is enough to keep the story alive.
The Terra Blade before hardmode. People swear old versions let you craft it early. They did not; the recipe always needed hardmode materials.
Every patch brings a new Shimmer duplication rumour. Some old versions did have real duplication bugs, which is why nobody ever fully stops believing the next one.
Carry a stack of blocks everywhere. Half of all Terraria deaths are fall damage.
Dig the hellevator early: straight down from base, a platform every few blocks so the fall does not kill you.
Keep a piggy bank and a safe in your inventory. Death takes what you are carrying, not what you have stored.
WX-78 can eat stale and spoiled food with no health or sanity penalty, which makes him the cheapest mouth to feed in the game.
The Celestial Portal swaps your character for a Moon Rock Idol, and you keep the map, the base and the inventory.
A beefalo herd can be walked across the whole map on hand-fed grass, but one in heat will attack the hand that feeds it.
Hound waves scale with days survived, and the growling starts a few seconds before they arrive. That is the whole warning.
The Pig King pays more gold for rarer trinkets, so it is worth sorting them before you trade.
Birds will not land while you are close, so a bird trap only works if you walk away from it.
Wormwood grows Living Logs from seeds, but he loses sanity every time he chops a tree.
Spoiled food is still food. Most characters can eat it for hunger at the cost of health, which beats starving.
A Lantern never runs out of fuel, which makes it the cheapest permanent light in the game.
Beefalo sleep at night, and you can shave a sleeping one for wool if you are quick enough to get close.
Glommer only appears at the Glommer statue on a full moon, and follows whoever is holding the flower.

Charlie is the thing in the dark. The radio, the shadow hands, the fact that night attacks you instead of just draining you: the community reading is that Maxwell's old assistant became the night. Klei has never confirmed it.
The Nightmare Throne. Sitting on it ends the run, and players have argued for years about whether the figure left sitting there is the player or the next victim.
There is a story that you can see the Grue if you stand in the dark long enough. What actually happens is that you die; the sighting is the death animation.
“They”. Characters mention Them, the throne belongs to Them, and nobody has ever seen Them. The strongest lore thread in the game is the one with no answer at all.
Wes is cursed. He is a mime who cannot speak, and the story that Maxwell did it to him has been repeated for years without anyone at Klei confirming it.
Fight in the light or do not fight. Night is for walking, not battles.
One meat plus three berries is Meatballs, and Meatballs solves most hunger problems.
Build the panic room before the first hound wave, not after it.
